newsitem.title: USA: UAW members ratify American Axle agreement.
newsitem.headline: UAW members ratify American Axle agreement.

text.p: A new three year agreement between the United Auto Wokers and American Axle Manufacturing Inc. was ratified by more than 97 percent of those who voted, the union announced Wednesday.

UAW officials said the contract, which covers about 7,200 workers at five plants in Michigan and New York, closely mirrors the terms in the pattern agreement reached with the Big Three automakers last fall.
UAW members will receive an up-front $2,000 lump-sum payment, followed by 3 percent general wage increases in September 1997 and September 1998.

The deal includes the same guarantee to maintain employment at 95 percent of the current workforce, a cost-of-living allowance, and $1,000 a year in tuition assistance for each dependent child enrolled in an accredited college or post-secondary technical school.
American Axle had demanded a lower starting wage for new hires, saying it needed the concessions to compete with non-union competitors, which pay less.

But new workers will be hired at 70 percent of the base wage, and reach the full amount in 36 months, the same as the Big Three. The starting base wage for an assembler in the American Axle contract is also the same for autoworkers, about $19 an hour.

The company was spun off from General Motors Corp. in 1994. It is the primary supplier of axles for GM pickup trucks and sport utility vehicles, and also makes products for Ford Motor Co. and Chrysler Corp.

The Amercian Axle negotiations were closely followed by the auto supply industry, where the UAW is trying to organise more plants. They were the first contract talks between the UAW and a GM spin-off. Workers were previously covered by the 1993-96 GM-UAW agreement.
"The new agreement reflects the vital role of UAW members in making this new company a profitable, competitive automotive supplier," said UAW President Stephen Yokich in a statement.
